topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the key learning outcomes, and establishes the conceptual framework of cancer evolution and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Mechanisms in Cancer Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tumors progress through the intrinsic interplay of Darwinian clonal selection and non-mutational epigenetic reprogramming.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of tissue hierarchies and stemness in tumor initiation, supported by experimental evidence from leukemia and colorectal cancer models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Stimuli and Inflammatory Promotion in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental cues and chronic inflammation act as promotional triggers that confer stem-like properties to permit tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Tumor-Microenvironment Dependencies, Spatial Profiling, and Evolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how established tumors depend on stromal interactions, the spatial technologies used to resolve them, and an overarching synthesis of tumor-microenvironment coevolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
